subtitle: Steel, Stone and Script: Chavundaraya’s Gift to Kannada

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Chavundaraya seated with palm-leaf manuscript in hand, distant outline of Shravanabelagola hill behind him under dawn light
panels.action: Chavundaraya sits cross-legged in a pillared hall, one hand resting on a bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts, while far behind him the rocky hill of Shravanabelagola rises under a pale dawn sky.

dialogue.text: Before his stone colossus rose on the hill, Chavundaraya carved another monument—an entire Jain universe, set not in Sanskrit, but in the new, daring prose of Kannada.

i18n.hi: पहाड़ पर पत्थर का विशालकाय उठने से पहले, चावुंदराय ने एक और स्मारक गढ़ा—पूरा जैन ब्रह्मांड, संस्कृत नहीं, नई साहसी कन्नड़ गद्य में।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high angle, showing battlefield memories dissolving into a quiet Jain monastery interior
panels.action: Half the frame shows a younger Chavundaraya in armor on a dusty battlefield, while the other half merges into an older Chavundaraya seated quietly in a Jain monastery hall, armor set aside beside him.

dialogue.text: He was known first for steel and strategy—a general of the Western Gangas, minister in Gangavadi, a man who had led armies and shaped courts.

i18n.hi: उन्हें पहले इस्पात और रणनीति के लिए जाना गया—पश्चिमी गंगा राज्य के सेनापति, गंगवाड़ी के मंत्री, सेनाएँ चलाने और दरबार गढ़ने वाला आदमी।

panels.shot: medium interior shot, Chavundaraya and Jain monks in discussion in a pillared mandapa, manuscripts spread before them
panels.action: In a stone-pillared hall, Chavundaraya leans forward in respectful conversation with Jain monks who sit among neatly stacked palm-leaf manuscripts and a simple wooden reading stand.

dialogue.text: Yet his mind turned more and more to the teachings he heard in the Jain basadis—the long stories of Tirthankaras and heroic laymen, preserved mostly in Sanskrit and Prakrit.

i18n.hi: फिर भी उनका मन बार‑बार जैन बसदियों में सुनी बातों की ओर लौटता—तीर्थंकरों और वीर श्रावकों की लम्बी कथाएँ, जो ज़्यादातर संस्कृत‑प्राकृत में सजी थीं।

panels.shot: close-up on Chavundaraya’s face, eyes intent on a palm-leaf manuscript inscribed in fine script
panels.action: Chavundaraya bends over a palm-leaf manuscript, his brow furrowed in thought as faint lines of script catch the light of an oil lamp beside him.

dialogue.text: The texts were vast, intricate, reverent—and distant from many in his own land, who spoke and thought in Kannada, not in courts’ languages.

i18n.hi: ये ग्रंथ विशाल, सूक्ष्म, श्रद्धापूर्ण थे—पर उनकी धरती के बहुतों से दूर, जो दरबारी भाषा नहीं, कन्नड़ में जीते‑सोचते थे।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind Chavundaraya, looking out onto a gathering of lay Jain householders in a courtyard
panels.action: From behind Chavundaraya’s shoulder, we see a courtyard of merchants, farmers and women seated on mats, listening to a monk, some straining and whispering whenever the discourse shifts into learned Sanskrit.

dialogue.speaker: chavundaraya
dialogue.text: The stories move them, but the words still stand at a distance.

i18n.hi: कथाएँ दिल छूतीं, पर शब्द अब भी दूरी बनाकर खड़े रहते।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chavundaraya speaking earnestly with an elder monk, a simple map of Gangavadi drawn on the floor between them
panels.action: Chavundaraya and an elder monk sit opposite each other on the floor; between them is a rough map of Gangavadi traced in chalk, dotted with villages and paths.

dialogue.text: He understood that texts did not live only in monasteries. They moved in markets and households, in the tongues people used daily.

i18n.hi: उन्हें समझ आया कि ग्रंथ सिर्फ मठों में नहीं जीते। वे बाज़ारों, घरों में, लोगों की रोज़ की ज़बान में चलते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle interior shot, Chavundaraya dictating while a scribe sits ready with stylus and palm leaf
panels.action: In a quiet chamber, Chavundaraya sits upright on a low platform, a scribe before him with stylus poised over a fresh palm leaf, listening for each measured word.

dialogue.text: Around 978, he made a deliberate choice: to retell Jain universal history in clear, flowing Kannada prose—what we now call the Chavundaraya Purana.

i18n.hi: लगभग ९७८ में उसने सोच‑समझकर कदम उठाया: जैन लौकिक इतिहास को साफ, बहती कन्नड़ गद्य में फिर सुनाना—जिसे आज हम चावुंदराय पुराण कहते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on the scribe’s hand as Kannada letters are incised, Chavundaraya’s hand seen gesturing rhythmically in the background
panels.action: The scribe’s hand carves neat Kannada characters into the leaf while, in soft focus, Chavundaraya’s hand moves in a steady rhythm as he dictates.

dialogue.text: Scholars will later see in this work a milestone of Old Kannada prose—a careful, almost austere style, carrying ancient narratives into a new language form.

i18n.hi: विद्वान बाद में इसे प्राचीन कन्नड़ गद्य का मील‑पत्थर मानेंगे—संयमी, सधा हुआ अंदाज़, जो पुराने आख्यानों को नए भाषा‑रूप में ढालता है।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot, faint ghosted scenes of Jain heroes and Tirthankaras behind Chavundaraya as he composes
panels.action: Behind the seated Chavundaraya, pale, dreamlike figures of Jain Tirthankaras, kings and lay heroes appear as overlapping silhouettes, suggesting the many lives his narrative threads together.

dialogue.text: He did not invent the universe he described; he condensed and arranged earlier Jain traditions into a single, accessible flow of teachers, conquerors, and renouncers.

i18n.hi: उसने यह ब्रह्मांड गढ़ा नहीं; उसने पहले की जैन परम्पराओं को समेट‑सँवारकर एक धारा बना दी—आचार्यों, विजेताओं और त्यागियों की।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chavundaraya pausing, looking out through a lattice window towards Shravanabelagola hill
panels.action: Chavundaraya pauses mid-dictation, turning his gaze through a carved stone window where the rocky outline of Shravanabelagola hill rises under the sun.

dialogue.text: His mind moved between page and stone. The same man who would raise the monolithic image at Shravanabelagola now also shaped a textual colossus for readers.

i18n.hi: उसका मन पन्ने और पत्थर के बीच दौड़ता रहा। जो आदमी श्रवणबेलगोला की एकाश्म प्रतिमा उठाएगा, वही पाठकों के लिए शब्दों का एक विशाल स्तम्भ भी खड़ा कर रहा था।

panels.shot: wide shot of a Jain teaching hall, laypeople gathered as a monk reads from a Kannada manuscript, Chavundaraya seated discreetly at the side
panels.action: In a crowded hall lit by afternoon light, a monk reads aloud from a Kannada manuscript while men and women listen intently; Chavundaraya sits quietly along the side wall, observing their faces.

dialogue.text: When the Purana was read aloud, its Kannada prose bridged the gap—listeners could now follow the long arc of Jain history with fewer intermediaries.

i18n.hi: जब पुराण का पाठ होता, उसकी कन्नड़ गद्य खाई पाट देती—सुनने वाले अब कम बिचौलियों के साथ जैन इतिहास की लम्बी धारा पकड़ लेते।

panels.shot: close-up on a listener, a merchant, repeating a key moral line softly, with Chavundaraya faintly visible in the background
panels.action: A middle-aged merchant sits cross-legged, lips moving softly as he repeats a moral line he has just heard, while behind him Chavundaraya’s figure watches, half in shadow.

dialogue.speaker: chavundaraya
dialogue.text: If they remember the restraint, the prose has done its work.

i18n.hi: अगर उन्हें उसकी संयमता याद रह जाए, तो गद्य ने अपना काम कर दिया।

panels.shot: interior study shot, Chavundaraya conferring with Nemichandra, manuscripts of doctrinal works between them
panels.action: In a quieter chamber, Chavundaraya sits opposite the Jain scholar Nemichandra, both leaning over bundles of manuscripts, indicating sections and discussing with calm intensity.

dialogue.text: Around him, other texts emerged. The Digambara scholar Nemichandra, working in the same milieu and under Chavundaraya’s patronage, composed doctrinal treatises like the Gommatasara.

i18n.hi: उसी समय और ग्रंथ भी उभरे। दिगंबर आचार्य नेमिचंद्र, जो उसी वातावरण में थे और चावुंदराय के आश्रय में, ने गोम्मटसार जैसे सिद्धान्त‑ग्रंथ रचे।

panels.shot: high-angle shot of several young students in a Jain school, one set reading from Chavundaraya Purana, another copying doctrinal verses
panels.action: In a simple schoolroom, young students sit in two rows, some reading aloud from Kannada prose leaves, others carefully copying verses from doctrinal texts under a teacher’s watchful eye.

dialogue.text: Together, narrative and doctrine shaped a learned world in Kannada—stories to inspire, treatises to instruct, both carried by the same expanding script.

i18n.hi: कथा और सिद्धान्त ने मिलकर कन्नड़ में एक विद्वत जगत गढ़ा—प्रेरणा के लिए कहानियाँ, सीख के लिए ग्रंथ, दोनों को वही बढ़ती लिपि ढो रही थी।

panels.shot: wide shot connecting stone and script: the Shravanabelagola colossus in the distance, in the foreground a monk holding the Kannada manuscript
panels.action: From a vantage point on the hill, the great standing figure at Shravanabelagola dominates the horizon, while in the foreground a monk sits with the Chavundaraya Purana manuscript resting on his knees.

dialogue.text: Historians will later warn us to separate authorship from patronage—to credit Nemichandra for his own works, and Chavundaraya for those he himself penned and fostered.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार बाद में चेताएँगे कि लेखक और आश्रयदाता को अलग‑अलग पहचानो—नेमिचंद्र को उनके ग्रंथों का श्रेय दो, और चावुंदराय को उनके लिखे‑संवारे कामों का।

panels.shot: close-up on a worn palm-leaf folio labelled by wear and patina, with a faint inscription hinting at its date
panels.action: A single palm-leaf folio lies on a wooden desk, its edges darkened with age, script lines faint but legible, while a small notation at the edge hints at its 10th-century origin.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars, from T.V. Venkatachala Sastry to Sheldon Pollock, will point to this Purana when they speak of how Kannada prose first took confident shape.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक विद्वान, टी. वी. वेंकटाचल शास्त्री से लेकर शेल्डन पॉलक तक, बताएँगे कि कन्नड़ गद्य ने पहली बार मज़बूत काया इसी पुराण में पाई।

panels.shot: medium shot of a contemporary researcher in a library gently handling the manuscript, with a ghostly overlay of Chavundaraya dictating
panels.action: In a present-day archive, a researcher bends over the preserved folios, while, like a faint echo, the image of Chavundaraya dictating appears above the page.

dialogue.text: They see in it a deliberate act of cultural policy by a minister-general: to give his own tongue the weight of scripture and history.

i18n.hi: वे इसे एक मंत्री‑सैनिक की सोची‑समझी सांस्कृतिक नीति मानते हैं: अपनी ही ज़बान को शास्त्र और इतिहास का वजन देना।

panels.shot: final wide shot, blending time: Chavundaraya seated with manuscript, behind him hints of modern Kannada bookshelves and cityscape
panels.action: Chavundaraya sits calmly with the Purana manuscript in his lap, while behind him the scene dissolves into shelves of modern Kannada books and a distant city skyline.

dialogue.text: His colossus in stone draws the eye, but his quieter monument endures in words: a reminder that when patrons give language the backing of power, that language can carry entire worlds forward.

i18n.hi: उसका पत्थर का विशालकाय आँखें खींच लेता है, पर उसका शांत स्मारक शब्दों में टिकता है: याद दिलाता है कि जब आश्रयदाता भाषा को सत्ता का सहारा देते हैं, तो वही भाषा पूरे‑पूरे जगत उठा ले जाती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Steel, Stone and Script: Chavundaraya’s Gift to Kannada
subtitle_i18n.hi: लोहा, पत्थर और लेखन: कन्नड़ को चावुंदराय की देन
